_note: 科研時事（站點級，跨科目）。顯示在三科總覽頁。cat 用 bio/chem/phys/math，只影響標籤顏色。越新的排越前。內容必須來自可靠來源並附連結——時事不是常識，寧可少寫也不要編。本檔由 scripts/fetch_news.py 自動抓取泛科學 RSS 產生，可手動補充。

items.t: 不是癌症卻同樣致命！耳朵痛癢伴隨臉歪嘴斜，當心致死率極高的「惡性外耳炎」
items.x: 「惡性外耳炎」並非癌症，而是致死率極高的嚴重耳道感染，細菌恐侵犯顱底與腦神經導致臉歪嘴斜。此病好發於高齡糖尿病患等免疫低下族群，若出現異常耳痛癢應盡速就醫。

items.t: SLAC 科學家發現了神秘的第三種磁性的確鑿證據
items.x: 近 90 年來，科學家一直認為磁性只分為兩類，但研究人員現在證實了第三種引人注目的類型，稱為交變磁性。他們利用專門的 X 射線發現了獨特的磁性特徵，證明這些材料的行為與傳統磁鐵不同。交變磁鐵將穩定性與有效攜帶訊息的能力結合在一起，有潛力
items.orig: SLAC scientists find conclusive proof of a mysterious third type of magnetism
items.origX: For nearly 90 years, scientists believed magnetism fell into just two categories, but researchers have now confirmed a remarkable third type called altermagnetism. Using specialized X-rays, they uncovered a unique magnetic signature that proves these materials behave differently from conventional magnets. Altermagnets combine stability with the ability to efficiently carry information, potentially overcoming major limitations in today's electronics. The discovery could lead to faster computers, more efficient data centers, and breakthroughs in quantum technology.

items.t: 麻省理工學院的科學家打破了 20 年的規則並解鎖了前所未見的晶體結構
items.x: 麻省理工学院的科学家挑战了二十年来的传统思维，发现灵活的分子连接，而不是刚性的分子连接，可以解锁排列纳米颗粒的全新方法。這項突破可能會催生出具有不同尋常特性的新一代設計材料，並在電子、醫學和能源領域得到應用。
items.orig: MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures
items.origX: MIT scientists have challenged two decades of conventional thinking by discovering that flexible molecular connections, rather than rigid ones, can unlock entirely new ways to arrange nanoparticles. The breakthrough could lead to a new generation of designer materials with unusual properties and applications in electronics, medicine, and energy.

items.t: 人工智慧揭示了一種隱藏的化學捷徑，可以將二氧化碳轉化為燃料
items.x: 科學家利用人工智慧發現了近 10,000 個將二氧化碳轉化為燃料和化學品的化學反應，揭示了傳統模型遺漏的關鍵途徑。這項發現極大地改善了對二氧化碳轉化的預測，並揭示了一種令人驚訝的氫反應，可以激發更高效的催化劑。
items.orig: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.origX: Scientists used artificial intelligence to uncover nearly 10,000 chemical reactions involved in transforming carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, revealing crucial pathways that traditional models had missed. The discovery dramatically improved predictions of CO2 conversion and uncovered a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.

items.t: 科學家發現了一個可以引發或破壞化學反應的隱藏因素
items.x: 研究人員發現了一個可以決定化學反應成功或失敗的隱藏因素，然後利用它將所需產物的比例從 16% 提高到 97%。透過控制電極附近的酸度，他們開發了一種很有前途的方法，使用氧氣和電力而不是添加危險的氧化劑來製造塑膠、藥品和其他產品的化學物質。
items.orig: Scientists discover a hidden factor that can make or break chemical reactions
items.origX: Researchers discovered a hidden factor that can determine whether chemical reactions succeed or fail, and then used it to boost the proportion of the desired product from 16% to 97%. By controlling acidity near electrodes, they developed a promising way to manufacture chemicals for plastics, medicines, and other products using oxygen and electricity instead of hazardous added oxidants.

items.t: 科學家可能終於解釋了為什麼我們的大腦和身體是交叉連結的
items.x: 科學家提出，大腦的神秘交叉線路（將每個半球與身體的另一側連接起來）可能起源於 5 億多年前的古代魚類的視覺系統。這種不尋常的安排可能只是在古老的基礎上建立新的大腦迴路的進化遺產，而不是為了特定的優勢而進化。
items.orig: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
items.origX: Scientists propose that the brain’s mysterious cross-wiring, which connects each hemisphere to the opposite side of the body, may have originated more than 500 million years ago in the visual systems of ancient fish. Rather than evolving for a specific advantage, this unusual arrangement may simply be a legacy of evolution building new brain circuits on an ancient foundation.

items.t: 埃及的古猿化石可能改寫人類起源的故事
items.x: 在埃及發現的一個 1700 至 1800 萬年前的猿類化石正在挑戰人們長期以來對人類和其他現代猿類祖先最初進化地點的看法。科學家現在懷疑北非和中東，而不是東非，可能是現代猿類進化的搖籃。
items.orig: Ancient ape fossil in Egypt could rewrite the story of human origins
items.origX: A 17- to 18-million-year-old ape fossil discovered in Egypt is challenging long-held beliefs about where the ancestors of humans and other modern apes first evolved. Scientists now suspect that North Africa and the Middle East, rather than East Africa, may have been the cradle of modern ape evolution.

items.t: 科學家剛發現了一個可以讓黑洞一分為二的漏洞
items.x: 科學家在通常阻止黑洞分裂的定律中發現了一個可能的漏洞，這表明旋轉極快的黑洞可能會一分為二。這項令人驚訝的發現提出了未來望遠鏡可能會偵測到的全新黑洞現象的可能性。
items.orig: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
items.origX: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.

items.t: 晶體中的微小缺陷揭示了巨大的量子驚喜
items.x: 研究人員解決了一個長期存在的挑戰，即了解鑽石和碳化矽等材料中的微小缺陷在光照下如何表現。他們的新計算方法揭示了碳化矽中一個令人驚訝的重要能量損失機制，而科學家之前卻低估了這個機制。這項發現有助於解釋多年來困擾研究人員的謎團，
items.orig: A tiny defect in a crystal reveals a big quantum surprise
items.origX: Researchers have solved a long-standing challenge in understanding how tiny defects in materials like diamond and silicon carbide behave when exposed to light. Their new computational method revealed a surprisingly important energy-loss mechanism in silicon carbide that scientists had previously underestimated. The finding helps explain a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years and could improve the design of quantum computers and sensors.
